indicators.note: something convertible can be changed into another form, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman's estate that can be turned into something else, like a sports car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convertible' reads as an adjective for a car or a building, but it tells you to rearrange ROMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is a landed estate with its house, a kind of property.

clue.text: The painter has to shake it up

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' says the pieces are read from the bottom of the light upwards

parts.note: to toss something is to shake or jerk it about
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist is told to stir things up a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TOSS IT round to give TISSOT; James Tissot was a French painter of Victorian society scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: James Tissot was a nineteenth-century French artist famous for his portraits of fashionable women.

clue.text: Force acquiring thousands by way of business

indicators.note: one word acquiring another takes it inside itself, so the second piece goes within the first

parts.note: to coerce someone is to force them
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them stand for thousands

explanation.surface: A company muscles its way into the big money through trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acquiring' puts MM inside COERCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce is trade, the buying and selling that makes up business.

clue.text: Bill will be paid for this

definitions.text: Bill will be paid for this

parts.words: Bill will be paid for this
parts.note: read 'Bill' as a man's name and it sounds like a bribe; read it as an invoice and the paper you get back once you have settled it is meant

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill is promised payment for a shady job.
explanation.walkthrough: The bill is the invoice, and once it is paid you are handed a slip acknowledging the payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A written acknowledgement of payment is given when an invoice is settled.

indicators.note: a reproduction is a copy made anew, here a remaking of the letters of the furniture style

explanation.surface: A copy of a Sheraton chair turns up among the main items of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheraton is an 18th-century English furniture style, and 'reproduction' suggests a copy of such a piece; it is the anagram signal. 'The main' is an old poetic word for the open ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is an old literary term for the ocean, and this is the body of water between Britain and Scandinavia.

clue.text: People are not fit to be given them

definitions.text: People are not fit to be given them

parts.words: People are not fit to be given them
parts.note: it sounds as if some people are unworthy to receive something; 'not fit' actually means unwell, and the sick are dosed with remedies

explanation.surface: Some people do not deserve to receive certain gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not fit' looks like a judgement on worthiness, but it means not in good health.
explanation.definitionFit: Drugs and remedies are what doctors prescribe for patients who are ill.

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly comes out of its usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Choir members surprise everyone by nodding off and snoring a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges the nine letters of SNORE A BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Baritones are male vocalists whose range lies between bass and tenor.

definitions.meaning: neat is an old word for cattle, and an ox or cow is something that moos
lesser in rank or position, below another

explanation.surface: Tidy, yet of poorer quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is not tidy but the old word for cattle, which low (moo).
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle make a mooing sound, so one is a beast that moos; a lesser rank is one placed further down.

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A rather noisy performance of songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' looks like an adverb modifying 'loud' (fairly loud), but it is an adjective meaning good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in its old sense means beautiful or good-looking.

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
the Somme is a river in northern France

explanation.surface: Someone looks into the route a river takes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' seems to be a river's course, but it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Consommé is a clear soup served as one dish of a meal.

clue.text: She'll set a good man free

parts.note: ST, for saint, is the crossword shorthand for a good man
to rid is to free or clear of something

explanation.surface: A woman promises to release a virtuous man from captivity.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'She', a girl's name; read the clue as 'She will set: A, good man, free' and the name is assembled from those pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrid is a Scandinavian female name, so it identifies a particular woman.

definitions.meaning: to move slightly or start to become active

explanation.surface: Get going once the weather turns colder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' is slang for a prison, which is also called stir.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir is to begin moving, and stir is also a slang word for jail.

clue.text: Drinks are of some help in this place

parts.note: ports are fortified wines
aid means help

explanation.surface: Someone claims a few glasses can be of use.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'this place' points to a town: the Egyptian port at the north end of the Suez Canal.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Said is an Egyptian city at the Mediterranean entrance to the Suez Canal, a location on the map.

parts.note: a bay is a horse with a reddish-brown coat
a diner who leaves food does not eat it

explanation.surface: A chestnut horse turns up its nose at the plants on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' is the verb of leaving food on the plate, but in the answer it becomes the noun for foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurel foliage used for flavouring stews is a common kitchen herb.

indicators.note: repairing something puts it back together, so these letters are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A workman whose job is fixing ladders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repairs' is the anagram signal on LADDERS; the craftsman actually makes and mends horse tack.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddler is a craftsman who makes and mends saddles and other riding gear.

clue.text: Little Sidney turned the lock, causing much trouble

indicators.note: turned means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Sid is the short form of the name Sidney
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A young boy turned the key in a door and caused a great deal of bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses SID to DIS; 'lock' is a lock of hair, not a door lock.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is great anguish or suffering, a severe kind of trouble.

clue.text: Show animal taken around totally unadorned

indicators.note: one piece taken around another encloses it, so the second sits inside the first

parts.note: a cat is an animal
bare means plain, wholly without decoration

explanation.surface: A creature is paraded in a display with no decoration whatever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken around' puts BARE inside CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a nightclub entertainment, a kind of stage show.

clue.text: A graduate register may be reduced

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
a table is a list or register

explanation.surface: A list of graduates might be trimmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase standing for an adjective: something that may be lessened.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate is to lessen, so an abatable tax or nuisance can be cut down.

indicators.note: letters set wrong are put out of their proper order, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hardships endured in old age are terribly unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges IN AGE SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Agonies are torments, acute physical or mental pains.

clue.text: Make a song about the whip cutting

indicators.note: one piece about another surrounds it, so the second goes inside the first

parts.note: to make a song is to sing
a lash is a whip

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fuss about being whipped and cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a song about' looks like the idiom for making a fuss, but 'about' puts LASH inside SING.
explanation.definitionFit: Slashing means making long cuts with a blade.

indicators.note: some of the word means just part of its letters are taken

explanation.surface: A small isle of outstanding beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes part of 'exceptionally'; the island is in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island in the Hebrides, known for its abbey.

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Something from the sea: a fish, or something made from algae.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is only a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a jelly extracted from red algae, used in cooking and laboratories.

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
a set is a group; the 's adds the S, as in set's

explanation.surface: A remark comparing something to a band's equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'group's' as SET'S, the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are things of value owned by a person or company, their resources.

parts.note: c, circa, is the abbreviation for about

indicators.note: round says the word for look is turned back to front

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: Inch around and glance about you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' reverses PEER to REEP after C.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep is to move slowly and stealthily, close to the ground.

clue.text: Serving men in a store can appear quite useless

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it

parts.note: a barn is a farm building for storing grain
the RE, Royal Engineers, are men serving in the British Army

explanation.surface: Soldiers stuck in a warehouse look completely idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts RE inside BARN; RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren land is unproductive, yielding nothing of value.

parts.note: 'beastly' sounds like an insult to a shabby vessel, but read literally it is a craft full of beasts, the ancient one that carried the animals two by two

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a horrible ancient tub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' means carrying beasts, not nasty: the Bible's vessel that held pairs of every animal through the Flood.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical vessel built to save the animals from the Flood is the oldest famous boat full of creatures.

indicators.note: the letters may be something else when rearranged, a loose signal to reorder them

explanation.surface: A gardener's note that the trees might be pruned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipped' suggests pruning, but it means curt in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipped speech is brief and abrupt, using few words.

clue.text: Important communication from the Soviet bloc?

definitions.meaning: a memorable or significant day is called this, from feast days marked in red on calendars
the communist countries were called Red, and a message from them would be a Red piece of correspondence

explanation.surface: A significant message arrives from behind the Iron Curtain.
explanation.walkthrough: Red is the colour of communism, so a letter from the Soviet bloc is literally red; the question mark flags that reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable day is called this after saints' days printed in red; Communist states were known as Red.
